full_judgment:
6. The Chairman of the Labour Court on a consideration of the evidence produced before him has come to the finding that the grievance petition was duly posted on the 6th December, 1969 and having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case it may be presumed that it duly reached the petitioner, as no contrary evidence was produced on behalf of the petitioner to rebut the presumption arising out of the facts of the case. The learned Chairman of the Labour Court has also come to finding on a consideration of the evidence on record that the letter dated the 2nd of December, 1969 in which respondent No. 2 is alleged to have confessed his guilt is not genuine and that it was not the willing expression of the mind of the petitioner. The learned Chairman of the Labour Court has come to a further finding that respondent No. 2 having made out a specific case that nobody approached him for taking over charge as directed by his superior officer and therefore he was unable to comply with the said order, and that no enquiry having been held by the authority concerned as to the correctness of the said case, there was, in the circumstances of the case, a clear violation of the principle of natural justice. It was ultimately held that on the facts of the case this was an appropriate case where an order for reinstatement in service should be made. 

 10. The Labour Court has come to the finding that the letter was posted on the 6th of December, 1969 and relying upon the presumption as to regularity of official acts has come to the conclusion that the letter must have been duly served upon the employer in due course. We think that this conclusion includes also that as to the service within the time as required under the provisions contained in section 25 of the Standing Orders Act. It is to be seen that the worker concerned brought his grievance to the notice of his employer in writing within 15 days from the occurrence, that is, by the 14th of December, 1969. The letter in question having been posted on the 6th of December, 1969 and the finding of the Labour Court being that ii reached the employer in due course, the conclusion is irresistable that it must have reached the employer before the 14th of December, 1969 who was residing in the same town since before the 14th of December, 1969. We, therefore, do not think that there is any force in this contention of the learned Advocate.
